::: {#def-identical-distributions .theorem}
## Identical structural distributions

Equivalent variables have identical structural equations and identically distributed error terms. Because equivalent variables read different units’ values, the equations are compared through their exposure mappings: for each covariate $\mathbf{X}_k$ there is one function $f_k$ with

$$
X_{ki}=f_k\big(g_{ik}(\cdot),U_{X_{ki}}\big)\ \text{ for every } i,\qquad X_{ki}\sim X_{kj}\ \Rightarrow\ U_{X_{ki}}\overset{d}{=}U_{X_{kj}},
$$

where $g_{ik}$ and $g_{jk}$ return the same quantities for units $i$ and $j$: their own values of the same constructs and, under interference, summaries given by the same component functions (C.19–C.20, C.25). See Remark 1.
:::
